name: Rust Grunt
description: The one enemy type the GDD asks for first: a Rust security officer in a slate uniform with a steel helmet and a cyan visor. Symmetrical, boxy and cold, a sharp contrast to Zed's warm, rounded look.
behaviour: Idles briefly after spawn, then chases Zed. Closes the lane gap first, and starts a strike once in range. At most two grunts may attack at once (attacker cap); the rest circle at a distance in neutral colours until a slot frees up.
telegraph: 450 ms wind-up: three-frame anticipation pose with the arm pulled back, the red telegraph icon pops above the head, the body tints red and the outline thickens. Then a quick 250 ms strike and a 700 ms recovery where it is open to a counter.
weakness: Low health and a slow recovery. Dodge or block the telegraphed strike, then punish during recovery with a light combo.

gddGap: GDD says one enemy type first and promises dynamic enemy behaviours later; difficulty comes from how waves arrive. A heavier bruiser gives waves a slow, high-threat piece to mix with grunts.
name: Rust Enforcer
description: A broader Rust officer in a squared-off slate vest with steel shoulder plates and a wide cyan visor. Same uniform language as the grunt, just bigger and blockier.
behaviour: Walks slowly and straight at Zed, ignores circling and takes an attacker slot whenever one is free. Throws one heavy overhand swing, then plants its feet during a long recovery.
telegraph: 600 ms wind-up with both fists raised overhead. Telegraph icon scaled up 1.4 times and a red ground danger ellipse at 30 percent alpha, per the heavy-enemy cue in the hit feedback spec.
weakness: Rewards dodging and defence: sidestep the swing, then land a combo in the long recovery window. Blocking works but the knockback is large.

gddGap: GDD lists dynamic enemy behaviours and defensive tools (block, dodge, parry) but gives no enemy roster. A fast, light attacker with a clear tell is a natural parry trainer.
name: Rust Baton Scout
description: A lean Rust officer in a slate uniform with a gunmetal baton and a narrow cyan visor. Straight lines, symmetrical stance, lighter than the grunt.
behaviour: Faster than the grunt and darts in for a quick poke, then backs off to the circle radius instead of standing around. Counts against the attacker cap like any other attacker.
telegraph: 320 ms wind-up: the baton is drawn back to the shoulder with a visible lean, red telegraph icon above the head. Short enough to feel quick, long enough to react to.
weakness: Fragile. A well-timed parry or a single combo opener ends the exchange; mashing without reading the tell gets punished by its speed.

gddGap: GDD asks for dynamic enemy behaviours and a player toolkit of block, dodge and parry. A ranged role forces the player to close distance and use lane movement, which melee-only enemies do not.
name: Rust Dart Marksman
description: A Rust officer in a slate uniform with a boxy gunmetal stun-dart launcher on one arm and a visor with a cyan aim line. Non-lethal gear: the dart only stuns and pushes back.
behaviour: Keeps to the far side of the arena and holds its distance, side-stepping away if Zed gets close. Fires one slow dart along its lane when it has an attacker slot, then reloads.
telegraph: 700 ms wind-up: raises the launcher, a cyan aim line draws along the floor toward Zed and the red telegraph icon pops above the head. The dart travels slowly enough to sidestep.
weakness: Step out of the lane to dodge, then rush it. Weak up close with low health and a long reload, so it rewards movement and juggle routes that carry Zed across the arena.

gddGap: GDD names block, dodge and parry as defence tools but never says which enemies reward them. A shielded elite makes the player use combos and juggles rather than button-mashing.
name: Rust Shield Sergeant
description: A Rust sergeant with a tall rectangular riot shield, steel helmet and a wide cyan visor. Symmetrical, squared-off and cold, with a gunmetal shield edge.
behaviour: Advances slowly behind the shield and blocks light hits from the front. Shield bash when the player is close, then drops the shield during recovery. Calls for an attacker slot before bashing so it never stacks with a full cap.
telegraph: 650 ms wind-up: shield pulled back and braced, red telegraph icon scaled up and a ground danger zone in front of it. Light attacks from the front bounce off the shield, which is also readable.
weakness: Heavy attacks break its guard and combos from behind or after a dodged bash land clean. Parry the bash to open the shield for a juggle.

gddGap: GDD promises dynamic enemy behaviours and says difficulty comes from how waves arrive, but names no support role. A Rust officer who buffs nearby grunts gives wave composition a priority target and rewards lane movement and juggle routes that reach the back line.
name: Rust Signal Warden
description: A Rust officer in a slate uniform with a boxy gunmetal radio pack and a short antenna, a steel helmet and a visor with a cyan indicator bar. Symmetrical and cold, with a squared-off stance that stays at the back of the group.
behaviour: Hangs back at the circle radius behind the grunts and never takes a melee attacker slot. Every few seconds it raises the radio to call a Rust order that speeds up grunts near it for a short time. If Zed closes in it side-steps away and only swats with a short baton jab when cornered.
telegraph: 600 ms wind-up for the radio call: arm raised with the radio, red telegraph icon above the head, and a cyan pulse ring on the floor around the grunts it will boost. The rare baton jab uses a 450 ms wind-up with the standard cues.
weakness: Fragile and always at the back. Rushing through the lane or using a juggle route to reach it cancels the call and removes the speed boost. Rewards crowd control and movement over standing still.
